section_summary: This section continues an intelligence monograph on Japanese activity in Latin America, concluding its survey of espionage networks, propagandists, schools, secret societies, and government controls in Argentina. It then assesses the small Japanese communities in Paraguay and Uruguay before beginning an extensive chapter on Japanese immigration, colonization, economic influence, political organization, propaganda, and suspected subversion in Brazil. Maps, demographic charts, landholding diagrams, and commercial statistics accompany the narrative.

subfiles.title: Japanese Monograph—Latin America: Argentina, Paraguay, Uruguay, and Brazil
subfiles.about: Continuation of a wartime intelligence survey of Japanese espionage, propaganda, immigration, colonization, commerce, and political influence in Argentina, Paraguay, Uruguay, and Brazil.
subfiles.summary: The Argentina portion completes accounts of Carlos Santa Cruz and Henri Catherin Gravet, describes the multinational JASPA espionage network, identifies clandestine mail channels and news correspondents, and discusses the Black Dragon Society, Japanese schools, arrests, and government controls. Separate country sections portray Paraguay's La Colmena colony as closely supervised by Japanese officials but economically weak, and Uruguay's small Japanese population as commercially active yet unsupported by evidence of organized espionage. The Brazil chapter charts Japanese population centers, landholdings, immigration mechanisms, colonization companies, cooperatives, propaganda, diplomatic and commercial organizations, and the extensive Japanese control alleged in Marília, Lins, Bastos, Registro, and surrounding agricultural districts. Maps and statistical graphics show population distribution, Axis nationals, national area comparisons, and Japanese-owned land.
